title: Area and Perimeter of Composite Shapes: Trapeziums, Kites and L-Shapes
seo_title: Year 8 Composite Area Worksheets: Trapeziums, Kites, L-Shapes and Paths (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: solve problems involving the area and perimeter of irregular and composite shapes using appropriate units
meta_desc: Free Year 8 maths worksheets on composite shapes for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M8M01): area of trapeziums, rhombuses and kites, perimeter and area of L-shapes, paths, borders and real-life problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Split a composite shape into simple shapes, or take a piece away from a bigger shape.
key_sub: Trapezium area = ½(a + b)h. Rhombus or kite area = ½ × product of the diagonals.
body_html:
How it works

A composite shape is made of simpler shapes. To find its area, split it into rectangles, triangles or trapeziums and add the areas, or find a bigger shape and subtract the part that is missing.

  • Trapezium: area = ½(a + b)h
  • Rhombus or kite: area = ½ × diagonal × diagonal

For the perimeter, add every outside edge. Work out missing lengths from the lengths you know.

Example

Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 4 cm and 8 cm and height 5 cm.

½ × (4 + 8) × 5 = ½ × 12 × 5.

Answer: 30 cm²

Example

A 1 m path goes round a lawn 10 m by 6 m. Find the area of the path.

Outside: 12 × 8 = 96 m².

Lawn: 10 × 6 = 60 m².

96 − 60.

Answer: 36 m²

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to halve in the trapezium or kite formula.
  • Using a slanted side instead of the perpendicular height.
  • Missing a side when finding the perimeter of an L-shape: there are 6 sides.
  • Adding the missing piece instead of taking it away.

faq.q: How do I find the area of a composite shape?
faq.a: Split it into rectangles, triangles or trapeziums and add their areas, or find the area of a bigger shape and subtract the missing part.

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a trapezium?
faq.a: Area = ½(a + b)h, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the perpendicular height.

faq.q: How do I find the area of a kite or rhombus?
faq.a: Multiply the two diagonals and halve the answer.

faq.q: How do I find the perimeter of an L-shape?
faq.a: Find any missing side lengths first, then add all six outside edges.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 20 cm. Which of these could be its area?
items.e: Length + width = 10. For example 6 × 4 = 24 cm². The largest possible area is 5 × 5 = 25 cm², so 40 and 100 are impossible.
